regeln: Align Visuals with Specific Script Cues: Every motif must show the exact person, object, or interaction mentioned; never substitute specific subjects with generic stock or unrelated reactions.
Deliver Title Payoffs and Key Terms: Ensure the script and visuals explicitly present and explain any specific nicknames, monikers, or core payoffs promised in the title.
Visualize Historical Specifics: Show the exact years, locations, and tangible outcomes mentioned in milestones rather than using vague, era-appropriate placeholders.
Maintain Signature Visual Identity: Use the channel-specific painted open-world-game style for fictional scenes; do not use generic AI art or stock footage.
Preserve Identity-Consistent Presenters: Always use the blue-eyed man with the fedora and gold watch for this channel; introduce him at the opening and bring him back in useful actions.
Apply Format-Specific Pacing: Use rapid-fire transitions (3-5s) for Shorts while allowing purposeful longer scenes in long-form videos; do not impose one format's speed on the other.
Adhere to Source Facts: Never override source-supported data, factual limits, or approved voice-overs with speculation, unverified claims, or personal interpretations.
Immediate Openings: Start videos immediately with the core subject and its factual cause, eliminating all vague teasers, transitions, or unrelated lead-ins.
Synchronize All Elements: Ensure that narration, visual motifs, and subtitle timing are perfectly synchronized for the entire duration of the video.
Use Mandatory Spoken CTAs: Include the required like, share, and save calls at the correct format-specific positions without substitution.
Extract General Habits from Feedback: Use reviews to derive general writing habits; phrase lessons from data conditionally and do not overgeneralize one image defect into a blanket ban.
Prioritize Concrete Fixes: Focus on observable production improvements; never claim a technique guarantees specific performance scores, retention, or 10/10 results.
